units.title: Holm clearance enters final days as owner stays silent
units.author: courier
units.text: The contract to clear Kittering Holm of trees reaches its last three days this week, with neither the contractor nor the island's owner willing to say how much of the work remains. Grieve Land Services was engaged to clear the 6 km island in 30 days, a schedule that people in the forestry trade have described to the Courier as unusually tight.

units.author: courier
units.text: From the harbour wall at Gilliver, residents report camp lights on the island most nights and regular trips by a contractor's workboat. Some fishermen say the island's southern end now shows open ground; others say the northern ridge looks much as it did. The Courier has not been able to verify either account, and the island is private land.

units.author: courier
units.text: A spokesperson for Ardent Vale Holdings said the company 'does not comment on the progress of private works' and referred questions to its contractor. Grieve Land Services said it was 'working to the agreed programme' and declined to discuss the crew, the size of the remaining work or the arrangements for leaving the island.

units.author: courier
units.text: Ammet District Council confirmed that the clearance consent remains valid for three years and that no further application relating to the island is pending. A council spokesperson said the authority had 'no role' in the timing of the contract and would not comment on reports about the owner's other property interests.

units.title: Lifeboat open day draws record crowd to Gilliver
units.author: courier
units.text: More than six hundred visitors crowded Gilliver harbour on Sunday for the lifeboat station's annual open day, the largest turnout in the station's records. Volunteers ran demonstrations of the inshore boat, a rope-throwing competition for children and a stall selling knitted lifeboat crews, which sold out by noon.

units.author: courier
units.text: The station's coxswain said the calm, bright weather had helped, and joked that 'half the Sound came to look at the island and stayed for the cake'. The day raised just over four thousand dollars towards a replacement launching tractor, which the station hopes to buy next spring.

units.author: courier
units.text: The winner of the under-twelves rope throw, a nine-year-old from Lisle, landed the line on the target buoy four times out of five. She told the Courier she had been practising on her grandfather's washing line, 'which he did not know about until now'.

units.title: Night faults 'tailing off', says power co-op
units.author: courier
units.text: Sound Power Co-op says the run of night-time faults that left parts of the Sound without electricity for much of the past fortnight appears to be ending. No unplanned outages were recorded on the Brackwater or Gilliver feeders over the weekend, the first fault-free nights since the problems began.

units.author: courier
units.text: The co-op has attributed the faults to corrosion from salt-laden fog on overhead equipment, and says replacement insulators have now been fitted on the worst-affected spans. Some line workers have questioned that explanation in online forums. The co-op said it 'does not comment on individual staff' and stood by its findings.

units.author: courier
units.text: Customers who lost food during the outages can still claim a fixed payment through the co-op's website until the end of next month. A spokesperson said more than nine hundred claims had been received so far, most of them for the contents of freezers.

units.title: Live: Carrow Point road closed after lorry sheds load
units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:05: The coast road below Carrow Point is closed in both directions after a flatbed lorry shed part of its load of timber pallets on the bend by the lighthouse lane. Nobody has been hurt. Police ask drivers to use the Tollinby road for now.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 12:35: A listener at the scene says roughly forty pallets are across both lanes and down the verge, with a few on the beach below. The driver is helping to stack them. A council crew with a loader is on its way from Port Ammet.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 13:25: The school bus for Carrow Point children will turn at the Tollinby junction this afternoon. Parents are asked to collect from the junction lay-by at 15:40. The school says it has phoned every family affected.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 14:30: The loader has cleared one lane and traffic is moving under a stop-go board. Several listeners have asked whether they can take the damaged pallets for firewood. The haulier says yes, once the road is clear, and 'please don't climb down to the beach for them'.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: 15:50: The coast road has fully reopened. The council says the verge will be tidied tomorrow morning. The last pallets on the beach are being left for the high tide to lift, which the coastguard says is not ideal but is the safest option. That's the end of our updates.

units.title: Dellow Court landlord to remove disused shop chiller
units.author: weypost
units.text: The managing agent of Dellow Court, the 14-storey tower block in north Weyhaven, has agreed to remove a disused refrigeration unit from the building's eighth-floor bin store after residents complained it was a fire risk and an obstruction. The unit belonged to the ground-floor shop and has been unplugged since the spring.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The chiller had been mentioned in a long-running residents' debate about noises in the block's stairwell, where lighting faults between the sixth and eighth floors were repaired earlier this month. A Kerrow Estates spokesperson said the removal was 'routine housekeeping' and 'not connected to any other matter'.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The residents' association secretary said she welcomed the decision, adding that the bin store had 'enough in it already without a fridge the size of a wardrobe'. Removal is expected within a fortnight, and the shop owner has offered to help carry it out.

units.title: Night bus cuts confirmed for winter timetable
units.author: weypost
units.text: Three of Weyhaven's five overnight bus routes will run hourly rather than every half hour from next month, the city transport board has confirmed. The board said falling passenger numbers after midnight, particularly during the recent power cuts, had made the half-hourly service hard to justify.

units.author: weypost
units.text: Shift workers' groups criticised the decision. A cleaner at the city bus depot told the Post that many night workers 'would rather wait inside the depot than at a dark stop for an hour', and asked for shelters on the cut routes to be properly lit before the change.

units.author: weypost
units.text: The transport board said it would review shelter lighting on all night routes over the winter and that the 38 and the harbour circular would keep their current frequency. The changes will be reviewed again in the spring.

units.title: Thirty days on the Holm: what happens at the deadline?
units.author: tradejournal
units.text: As Grieve Land Services approaches the end of its 30-day clearance contract on Kittering Holm, attention in the trade is turning to what happens if the work is not finished on time. Neither Grieve nor the client, Ardent Vale Holdings, has published the contract terms, and both declined to comment for this article.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Two contracts managers at other firms, speaking generally, said fixed-term clearance contracts usually include either a penalty per day of overrun or a clause allowing the client to bring in another contractor to finish. 'Thirty days is a headline number,' one said. 'What matters is what the small print says happens on day thirty-one, and nobody outside the room knows that.'

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: The per-tree rate reported at the start of the contract, a hundred dollars a stem plus day rates for crew, is generous by regional standards. One estimator suggested the premium reflected the logistics of an island with no road access rather than any unusual risk, and said it was 'the sort of job you price for the boat, not the trees'.

units.author: tradejournal
units.text: Grieve has not said how much of the island has been cleared. Observers on the mainland offer estimates ranging from 'a little over half' to 'nearly all', none of them verifiable. The Journal will report the outcome when either party is willing to discuss it.

units.title: Night ferry floodlights 'here to stay', Sound Lines says
units.author: soundfm
units.text: The extra deck and slipway lighting fitted to Sound Lines' night ferry last week will stay in place permanently, the operator has confirmed. The floodlights were introduced when night crossings resumed after a crew welfare review that cut the late-evening service for almost a week.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: A Sound Lines spokesperson said crews had found the lighting 'made berthing in poor visibility much easier' and that passengers had welcomed it. The harbour office at Gilliver says it is looking at matching lights on the slipway itself, subject to funding.

units.author: soundfm
units.text: Asked about recent claims that one of the reported slipway sightings was a prank by a local teenager, the operator said it 'does not comment on individual incidents' and that the lighting was 'about safety, full stop'.

units.title: Lisle school roof: funding finally approved
units.author: courier
units.text: Lisle's primary school will get a new roof next summer after the district council approved funding at its finance committee on Monday. The school's hall has been out of use on wet days for two years because of leaks, with buckets a familiar sight at assemblies.

units.author: courier
units.text: The head teacher said pupils had grown so used to the buckets that the youngest class had named them. A former teacher at the school, who taught there for more than three decades, said the roof had 'leaked in exactly the same place in 1991, and we were promised a new one then'.

units.author: courier
units.text: Work will be timed for the summer holidays so that the ferry can carry materials across without disrupting the school run. The council said it expects the contract to go out to tender in the new year.

units.title: Marrow Sound forecast, 28th
units.author: met
units.text: High pressure building from the north. Today: dry and bright, sunny spells, light northerly winds. Maximum 7 degrees. Tonight: clear and very cold, widespread frost, a few freezing fog patches inland around Brackwater by dawn. Minimum minus 3 inland, 1 on the coast. Outlook: settled and cold through the weekend.

units.title: Inshore waters, Carrow Point to Weyhaven
units.author: met
units.text: Inshore waters forecast, valid 24 hours. Wind north or northeast 2 to 3, occasionally 4 in the south. Sea state smooth or slight. Weather fair. Visibility good, occasionally moderate in sea smoke near coasts at dawn. No warnings in force.

units.title: Tide times, Gilliver, 28th
units.author: met
units.text: Gilliver tides: high water 04:52 (4.1 m) and 17:14 (4.3 m); low water 11:03 (0.9 m) and 23:30 (0.8 m). Neap tides building to springs early next week. Half-tide windows for small landings around 08:00 and 14:10.

units.title: Yellow warning: ice, inland areas
units.author: met
units.text: Yellow warning for ice, valid 22:00 tonight to 10:00 tomorrow, inland areas including Brackwater and Tollinby. Untreated roads, pavements and cycle paths will be icy after a clear night. Take extra care on the reservoir lane and the Tollinby road, where surfaces are freshly laid.

units.title: Service update, 28th
units.author: ferry
units.text: All Sound Lines sailings between Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver are running to the published timetable today, including the 22:40 night crossing. Passengers are reminded that ramps and pontoons may be icy early and late in the day. Please use the handrails.

units.title: Night crossings: deck lighting retained
units.author: ferry
units.text: Customer notice: the additional deck and slipway floodlighting introduced on night crossings will now be retained permanently. Passengers boarding after dark should wait behind the yellow line until the ramp is lowered and the crew signal to board. Thank you for your patience during recent changes.

units.title: Restoration complete: Gilliver coastal feeder
units.author: power
units.text: Sound Power Co-op: insulator replacement on the Gilliver coastal feeder is complete and the feeder has been returned to normal running arrangements. No interruptions were recorded overnight. Customers on this feeder who lost supply in the last fortnight can find the compensation form on our website.

units.title: Planned work: Tollinby north, 30th
units.author: power
units.text: Planned interruption: Tollinby north (Mill Lane, Orchard Rise, the industrial estate) on the 30th from 09:00 to 13:00, to replace a pole-mounted transformer. Affected customers have been sent letters. Please switch off sensitive equipment before 09:00.

units.title: Waste collections: catch-up schedule
units.author: council
units.text: Recycling collections missed during the recent power works will be caught up as follows: Port Ammet town centre and Rope Walk, Wednesday; Tollinby, Thursday; Lisle, by the Friday ferry. Please leave boxes out and lidded. We apologise for the delay and thank residents for their patience.

units.title: Road reopened: Brackwater junction
units.author: council
units.text: The Brackwater junction on the Tollinby road has reopened following resurfacing. The junction now operates as a give-way. Road markings will be completed when temperatures allow. Drivers are asked to approach with care while the new surface beds in.

units.title: Water mains flushing, Lisle
units.author: council
units.text: Mains flushing will take place in Lisle village on the 29th between 10:00 and 15:00. Some customers may notice low pressure or slightly discoloured water. This is harmless; run the cold tap until the water is clear. Please avoid washing pale laundry during these hours.

units.title: Notice to mariners: temporary light, Kittering Holm landing stage
units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. The private temporary light exhibited at the Kittering Holm landing stage, flashing yellow every 5 seconds, will continue to be exhibited until further notice. Mariners are reminded that the landing stage is private and that the approach dries at low water springs.

units.title: Buoy relit: Carrow Point south cardinal
units.author: coast
units.text: Notice to mariners. The Carrow Point south cardinal buoy, reported unlit last week, has been relit and is operating normally, quick flashing six plus one long every 15 seconds. Thank you to the vessels that reported it.

units.title: Small craft: sea smoke near coasts
units.author: coast
units.text: Advice to small craft. With very cold air over relatively warm water, sea smoke is likely in sheltered inlets and harbours around dawn over the next few days. Visibility in sea smoke can fall below 100 metres. Use navigation lights and sound signals, and reduce speed.

units.title: Holm timber camp, clerk's diary: December entries (transcribed)
units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec 9th. Wind NE, hard frost. Tally 41 stems the north line, 38 the east. Wages paid to the 7th, all present. McRory's hand much better. The men will not go to the far lines after the lamps are lit and I have ceased to argue it, the foreman agreeing. Bread short; boat looked for Thursday. [Transcriber: 'McRory' is spelt three ways in this volume.]

units.author: camp_clerk_1894
units.text: Dec 11th. No boat. Calm & very cold. Tally 22 stems, the light failing by three. Two men asked to be put off at the next boat and I have entered them so. Lamps kept in all three huts till morning by the foreman's order, oil to be noted against stores. The sea quiet as a pond. The Psalm for the evening, the 121st.

units.title: Carrow Point light, keeper's log: middle watch excerpts (later volume)
units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan 14. 00:00 wind SW 3, visibility good, lamp trimmed. 02:00 same, glass steady. 03:30 lamp checked, burning well. Remarks: walkers on the shore road again, two, by the gate. Did not answer. Assistant keeper saw them also and asks that it be noted that he saw them.

units.author: carrow_keeper
units.text: Jan 17. 00:00 calm, frost, visibility excellent. 02:00 lamp checked. 04:00 lamp checked. Remarks: Assistant keeper Dunmore has asked to put in for transfer to a rock station, which I have forwarded with a fair character. He gives no reason in his letter and I have not pressed him. Nothing on the road tonight.

units.title: Notebook of a survey of the islands, 1923: the Holm (later pages)
units.author: naturalist_1923
units.text: Day six. Browse heavy on holly and bramble along the north ridge, leaders nipped at a height I would put down to deer anywhere else. No slots, no droppings, no lying-up places in the bracken. Hares plentiful (Lepus marrowensis, provisionally). [Sketch: a nipped holly shoot, scale in inches.] Boatman again declines to stay the night; he will fetch me at four. I find I don't argue with him.

units.title: A Gilliver fisherman's diary, 1930s: the hard winter
units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 3. Wind east. Stayed in. Mended two creels. Herring 4 shillings the cran at Port Ammet which is robbery. Mother kept the lamp on the sill all night, said the wind would want it. Tam would not go out, says the Holm side is no good this week. I said its no worse than any week. He said leave it.

units.author: fisher_diary_1930s
units.text: Feb 6. Calm at last. Went out alone, Tam stayed back. Fair catch on the Lisle side. Did not go round the Holm, not for Tams sake, the tide was wrong. Seen lights low on the Holm shore at dusk which must be some boat in close. Nobody owns to it at the pier.

units.title: Talk: Kittering Holm timber camp (1890s)
units.author: hist_wiki_pell
units.text: Following yesterday's concession on wages, a correspondent asks whether I now accept the 'lamp rule' explanation for the camp's end. I do not. 'Would not go to the far lines after the lamps' describes a rule, not a reason. Camps had rules about dark work for the plain reason that men with axes injure each other in the dark. [This claim is poorly sourced, but it has the merit of being boring.] Pell

units.title: Gilliver window lamp (custom): recent observance
units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: Since the autumn of this year the custom has again been widely observed in Gilliver, with lamps reported in most seaward windows on the harbour front (personal observation of the editor; not yet a society survey). Earlier periods of wide observance are recorded in the 1890s and 1930s [citation needed: the 1930s date rests on a single diary]. The society makes no claim about the reasons for the present revival.

units.title: Oral history project, Gilliver, 1974: tape 11 (two speakers)
units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: INTERVIEWER: Why did your mother keep the lamp? SPEAKER A: For the boats. Everybody'll tell you for the boats. My father was on the boats and she kept it for him. [pause] Well. She kept it after he came off them, too. I suppose she was used to it. You get used to a thing.

units.author: oral_history_1970s
units.text: INTERVIEWER: And you, Mrs [name withheld]? SPEAKER B: Not for the boats. Boats have the light at Carrow. It was so they'd know the house was awake. That's what my gran said. INTERVIEWER: Who would know? SPEAKER B: [long pause] Whoever was passing. You don't ask that kind of thing, love. It's only manners.

units.title: Catalogue additions, week four
units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LBA-2210. Date: this month, day 21. Location: Brackwater reservoir, north inlet. Kit: handheld recorder, foam windshield. Duration 46 min. Description: still water, distant road traffic, tawny owl at 14:20 into the file. Percussive events: none. Curator's note: submitted by dunlin_rec with the comment 'for the archive, nothing in it'.

units.author: lowband_archivist
units.text: LBA-2214. Date unknown, probably 1980s (cassette label 'BW gate, nights'). Location: Brackwater estate, presumed. Kit unknown, mono. Duration 31 min. Description: wind in conifers, a gate chain, two percussive events at 08:12 and 08:14 into the tape, unattributed. From a donor's attic collection. Curator's note: the label is in pencil and may not refer to this recording.

units.title: From the 'Gilliver Notes' column (undated, c. 1890s)
units.author: courier_1890s
units.text: The lamps of Gilliver have been much remarked upon this winter by visitors from Port Ammet, who find our harbour front 'lit like a feast day' at all hours. Your correspondent assures them it is no feast but an old courtesy, and that the oil merchant is the only party who profits by it. Some say the custom grew up with the timber men's return; others that it is far older. Your correspondent heard both in one evening, from the same gentleman.

units.title: Relay station survey, Kittering Holm: Appendix C (stores and transport)
units.author: relay_engineer_1950s
units.text: Appendix C. Stores to be landed at the south landing at half tide only; low-water landing not advised. Daily transport: survey party of four embarked 07:30, taken off by 15:45, as requested by the party (see paragraph 14). Fuel for a permanent station estimated at 900 gallons per annum. A resident staff of two would require relief at fortnightly intervals at minimum.

units.title: Editor's note: the winter reels of the early 1930s
units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: Editor's note. Readers asking for the Courier's coverage of the hard winter of the early 1930s will find the January and February issues on reel 1931-A, now digitised. The paper that winter is mostly concerned with herring prices, a disputed harbour levy and a church roof. There is one short paragraph about lamps in Gilliver windows, reproduced below. We have not verified the correspondent's figures.

units.author: courier_archivist
units.text: From the issue of 12 February, page 6: 'Gilliver keeps its lamps lit through these long nights, and your correspondent counted forty-one upon the harbour front on Tuesday last, a number the oldest inhabitants say has not been seen since their own childhood. The oil merchant reports brisk trade, and asks that customers bring their own cans.'

units.title: Payroll statement GLS-PR-2808: contract days 22-28
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Statement ref: GLS-PR-2808. Site: KH-01 Kittering Holm. Period: contract days 22 to 28. Itemised day-rate and per-unit lines are shown on the site account. The next statement will be issued at contract close. This mailbox is not monitored; please direct queries to your operations manager.

units.title: Reminder: outstanding crew wages, KH-01
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: AUTOMATED REMINDER. Account: KH-01. Status: crew wages outstanding. Balances outstanding at contract close must be cleared before the final contract payment can be released. Reference: ARR-KH01-28. This is a system-generated notice. Replies to this address are not read.

units.title: Leaver processed: KH-01 headcount updated
units.author: grieve_payroll
units.text: GRIEVE LAND SERVICES, PAYROLL. Notification type: leaver processed. Site: KH-01. The leaver's day-rate line has been closed and final pay calculated to the leaving date. Site headcount for the final statement has been updated. No action is required from site. This mailbox is not monitored.

units.title: Your policy LY-4471-0938: renewal in 30 days
units.author: lyle_insurance
units.text: Lyle Insurance. Your policy LY-4471-0938 renews in 30 days. Your current cover includes personal accident and belongings away from home. Please tell us if your circumstances have changed, including remote, island or offshore work, as some activities need additional cover. Peace of mind, wherever the work takes you. Terms and exclusions apply; see your policy booklet, section 7.

units.title: Frost is here! Five ways to keep your camp cosy
units.author: camp_supply_news
units.text: Frost is here! Five ways to keep your camp cosy: 1) Insulate the floor before the walls! 2) Keep your lantern topped up, because a dark camp is a cold camp! 3) Dry boots upside down near, not on, the stove! 4) A flask by the bed beats a cold kitchen at 3am! 5) Stock up early, before the boats get busy! Hearthglow lanterns, still the brightest in the Sound, now 15% off until Sunday!

units.title: End of contract: boats and paperwork
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, a few things for the last stretch: - Supply boat runs as normal on the 29th and 30th, off Gilliver berth 3 at 06:30, back across mid-morning. - Please have empties, skips and the waste oil drums on the landing stage by 07:30 both days so the skipper isn't waiting. - Timesheets for days 22 to 30 to me by the 30th; photos are fine. - Demob and crew transfer details I'm still confirming with the client. I'll send them as soon as I have them. Thanks, Ruth

units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, forgot one thing: the skipper says the landing stage is best at half tide on the 29th, around 08:00, and he would rather not wait for the afternoon one. Load accordingly. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Numbers
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, numbers look strong from the last return. Head office is pleased, which you'll appreciate is rare enough that I'm writing it down. Keep it steady and safe for the last days, please, and no heroics on the big stems. A tidy finish matters more to the client than a fast one. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Just checking where we are
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, just checking where we are on numbers. From the last return there is still a gap to close before the 30th, and head office has asked me about it twice today. I'm not going to tell you how to run your site. If anything on the boat would help, extra chain, files, fuel, put a list in with the empties and the skipper will bring it to me. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Crew pay before the 30th
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, payroll's reminder will have reached you this morning. I'll only add that the final contract payment can't be released while crew wages are outstanding on the account, and that's not something I can argue round. I know it's been a long month. Please clear it before the 30th if you possibly can. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Headcount for the final days
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, head office has updated the headcount for the final days to reflect the leaver, so the day-rate total on the closing statement will be lower. I haven't found anyone to fill the place this late and I've stopped trying. If the rest of the crew need anything for the last stretch, the boat is the way. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: Your truck and the barge
units.author: ruth_imber
units.text: Hi, one for the paperwork: if the truck on site is yours rather than hire, it will need its own slot on the barge after the contract. The barge is booked by the company for company plant. I've asked whether a private vehicle can go on the same crossing but I can't promise a date yet. Thanks, Ruth

units.title: The end of the contract (questions, no obligation)
units.author: nell_ashdown
units.text: Hello again. I'm writing a short piece on the end of the Holm contract for Friday's paper. As before, I don't expect a reply. If you can: 1. Is the crew expected to leave the island on the 30th, or later? 2. Has Grieve told you what happens if the work isn't finished? 3. Is everyone well? I've put the same questions to Grieve and Ardent Vale. Anything you say can be unattributed. Best wishes, Nell Ashdown, The Ammet Courier

units.title: What do you call a tree with no deadline?
units.author: hal_brannock
units.text: Chief. Answer: a tree. Couldn't think of a better one, it's been a week. The road job's stopped for frost and they're paying us to sit in the site cabin doing paperwork, which is my idea of hell, with biscuits. You're nearly at the end. Count your saws, count your people, get on the boat. That's all. Hal

units.title: the play, the dog, Mum
units.author: sam
units.text: hi you. the play's finished and the costume is in the wash and she is still saying her lines at breakfast, including the extra one nobody wrote. Mum came to the last night with her frame and sat on the end so she could stretch the leg out, and told the teacher it was better than the telly. the dog ate half a programme in the car. anyway. the paper says your job ends on the 30th. does that mean you're home on the 31st? nobody tells me anything. is it really fine out there? love, S x

units.author: sam
units.text: can't sleep. stupid really. there was a photo in the paper tonight of Gilliver after dark with a lamp in nearly every window, and I thought of you out there with your one camper light. I know you'll say it's fine. just tell someone to tell me when you're on the boat, all right? love, S x

units.title: Sorry, it's me again
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, sorry, it's me again. I won't keep you. I just wanted to say I'm fine, work is fine, the new dentist is very slow but very kind to the nervous ones. If Tomas asks, I've been sleeping. Is he sleeping? He never says. Sorry for writing so late in the evening. Ana

units.title: Is Tomas all right?
units.author: ana_reyner
units.text: Hello, I'm sorry to write twice in one evening. I still can't get a straight answer from anyone at Grieve about who left the crew. If it wasn't Tomas, is he all right? If it was, I suppose I'll know soon enough when he turns up at my door with his washing. Either way, please tell him I'm fine. Sorry. Ana

units.title: the jetty light
units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Hello again. Sorry, I said I would stop writing so often and I haven't. I only wanted to say that the light on your jetty stayed on all last night, and that I think that's good. My mother used to say a light left on means someone is minding the house. I might be wrong to tell you that. You don't have to read this. M.
